title: The Pilot Who Escorted an Enemy Bomber Home
notes: Register: warm, and it is earned. The first half is plain so the warmth at the end has somewhere to come from. The reunion is the ending; do not lean on it early.

No free photograph of the encounter exists. Nothing generated shows either aircraft, or the two aircraft together; on maps the bomber and the fighter are small tokens. Brown and Stigler appear as vague-faced cartoons only OUTSIDE the encounter (their early lives, the search, the reunion), never during the mission or in a cockpit.

The widely shared painting of Stigler's Bf 109 beside the B-17 (Nicolas Trudgian, 'A Higher Call') is on Commons marked CC0, but it is a commercial artwork and a reconstruction of the event. Do not use it.
All aircraft photographs are of other B-17s and Bf 109s and are captioned so they do not read as Ye Olde Pub or Stigler's aircraft.
The crew photograph (p07) includes Hugh Eckenrode, who was killed on this mission. It is shown as the crew, without comment.
Real decorations (the Knight's Cross, the Air Force Cross, the Silver Star) are not generated: they appear as a plain medal silhouette with their names set as type.
What is documented and what rests on memory: the script says so at s28, s36-s37 and s46-s47. On-screen type keeps the same distinction: 'by his account', 'another account', 'records'.
Music is null for the build. If a bed is added in the edit, nothing under the encounter (s27 to s47); a low, sparse bed may enter at s48 and carry the reunion.
LOW RESOLUTION: p03, p05, p07, p12, p14. Native size only.
Every archival URL was resolved from the Commons API.
Guide objects: the parachute pack (Rödel's rule, s25 and s32) and the empty sky over the sea (s05, s33, s41).

brown.desc: Charlie Brown: at 21 a young American bomber pilot in a 1943 USAAF leather flight jacket and crush cap; later in a 1980s suit; in old age in a windbreaker; simple vague face

stigler.desc: Franz Stigler: as a boy with a glider; as a 1930s flying instructor in a leather jacket; as a post-war mechanic in Canada; in old age in a cardigan; simple vague face

crowd.desc: extras: a 1986 audience of veteran pilots in a hall, elderly former aircrew at a reunion, simple vague faces
